title: Summit Point-of-Sale Pilot Orientation & Acceptance Brief
content:
Purpose:

This brief prepares the Redwood SE + Summit Retail teams for the upcoming 6-week pilot that embeds Redwood inference into Summit’s in-store point-of-sale (POS) assistant. Goal: validate production latency/cost profile and operational handoff criteria so Summit can decide on Dedicated capacity purchase or Private deployment.

Background / short context:
- Summit Retail (pilot group: 24 stores in Pacific Northwest) wants an LLM-based cashier assist to: item lookup, cross-sell suggestions, and refund guidance.
- Team constraint: average POS transaction latency budget = 150ms for LLM step (end-to-end token generation), peak concurrency during weekend evening shifts.
- Data constraints: PII in transaction notes; Summit requires audit logs and KMS integration for model inputs/outputs.

Primary stakeholders:
- Summit Retail: Evan Brooks (Customer Eng), Priya Nair (Head of Retail Ops), Jordan Lee (Store IT)
- Redwood: Maya Chen (SE lead / owner), Jared Patel (integration lead), Riley Adams (runtime engineer), Sofia Martinez (security/compliance)
- GTM contact: Ana Ruiz (account executive)

Pilot objectives (measurable):
1) Latency: 95th percentile LLM response time <= 180ms for 90% of transactions in normal load (definition below).
2) Cost: average inference spend per 1k transactions <= $X (commercial sensitive — referenced in contract).
3) Quality: cross-sell suggestion CTR >= 4% (measured via A/B in pilot stores).
4) Reliability: target 99.5% successful LLM responses (no errors/500s) during business hours.
5) Security/compliance: end-to-end encryption in transit + KMS-managed keys for logs; no persisted unredacted PII in Redwood logs (verified by audit test).

Success criteria (Acceptance matrix) — each criterion must be green for pilot signoff:
- Performance: measured ramp test (see timeline) shows sustained 95p <= 180ms and tail behavior documented (latency histogram).
- Cost forecast accuracy: Redwood cost model < +/- 12% vs pilot spend.
- Functional: 500 randomly sampled suggestions from pilot pass Summit QA checklist: relevance >= 88% (human-labeled).
- Integration: POS adapter handles offline store mode gracefully (queued requests) with no data loss in 24h offline window.
- Security: penetration test scoped to POS adapter returns no critical findings; any high/mediums must have remediation plan with owners.

Scope (in):
- Integration of Redwood hosted inference endpoint via Summit POS adapter (Node.js microservice).
- Local caching of static prompts and prefix KV caching for repeated items.
- Instrumentation: tracing + per-request cost and latency tags shipped to Redwood Console.
- A/B scaffolding for CTR measurement (stores randomized).

Out of scope (for pilot):
- Full Private on-prem deployment (we will evaluate after pilot if signoff criteria met).
- Training/custom model finetuning — only prompt engineering and model selection from Redwood catalog.
- Offline-first native POS app rewrite.

Technical architecture overview (high-level):
- POS terminals -> POS adapter (in-store VM / Docker) -> Redwood Hosted API (region us-west2) -> Redwood Console telemetry.
- Optional: burst path to Dedicated pool if queued latency exceeds threshold (configurable).
- Secrets: POS adapter obtains ephemeral API key from Summit KMS, rotates nightly.

Data & security notes:
- Input scrubber: adapter will apply regex-based scrubber for card numbers and manually defined store-sensitive fields before send.
- Logging: by default, store-level transaction IDs only are logged; full payload logs are stored only in customer-managed S3 bucket if enabled (for debug, not enabled by default).
- Audit: SEs will run a controlled audit (50 random records) to verify no PII leakage into Redwood Console logs.

Integration checklist (initial):
- [ ] POS adapter repo forked and initial build pipeline created (owner: Jared)
- [ ] Endpoint credentials exchange established with Summit KMS (owner: Sophia/Customer Eng)
- [ ] Test harness for synthetic traffic (spike and sustained load) completed (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Instrumentation mapping: trace ids, cost tags, custom metrics (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Store A/B bucket assignment script deployed (owner: Summit IT)

Workshop (kickoff) agenda — 90 minutes (week 0):
- 0–5 min: Introductions + objectives (Maya)
- 5–20 min: Summit business context and pilot success definition (Evan / Priya)
- 20–35 min: Proposed integration pattern and security model (Jared + Sofia)
- 35–55 min: Latency & load shape expectations, load test plan (Riley)
- 55–70 min: Acceptance matrix walkthrough + metrics instrumentation (Maya)
- 70–85 min: Risk register and mitigation owners (group)
- 85–90 min: Immediate next steps / action owners (Ana)

Timeline & milestones (6-week pilot):
- Week 0: Kickoff workshop + quick repo bootstrap + credential handoff
- Week 1: Adapter initial integration + CI + basic smoke tests
- Week 2: Internal load testing and cost projection
- Week 3: Canary deployment to 3 pilot stores + begin A/B measurement
- Week 4: Ramp to 24 stores, observe 7-day window for stability
- Week 5: Data collection, quality labeling sample (500 items), cost reconciliation
- Week 6: Final acceptance runbook, security audit, pilot signoff decision meeting

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: tail latency spikes during weekend peaks. Mitigation: pre-configured fallback to smaller model variant + queue throttling and graceful degrade UX. Owner: Riley.
- Risk: PII slipping through scrubber for edge-case fields. Mitigation: extra scrubber pattern + manual review of audit sample. Owner: Sofia.
- Risk: Store network flakiness causing request backlog. Mitigation: adapter queue with durable persistence to local disk + replay. Owner: Jordan (Summit IT).

Measurement & telemetry plan:
- Key metrics streamed every minute to Redwood Console: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens generated, cost-per-request, error-rate by code.
- Business metric: cross-sell CTR tracked by Summit’s analytics — we will provide daily export and weekly join for pilots.

Acceptance signoff process:
- Compile automated reports (latency, errors, cost) + human QA sampling (quality) + security audit report.
- Weekly sync during pilot; final signoff meeting in Week 6 where Summit will mark criteria green/red.

Immediate action items (post-kickoff):
- Jared: create adapter feature branch and PR template (due in 48h)
- Riley: share synthetic load script and baseline runbook (due EOD Week 0)
- Sofia: produce scrubber patterns list and audit checklist (due in 3 days)
- Summit (Jordan): provide VPN/network details and list of 24 pilot store IDs (due in 72h)

Open questions / decisions needed from Summit:
- Confirm whether Summit wants debug payload logs captured to customer S3 during pilot (privacy tradeoff).
- Finalize cost threshold X used in contract (affects cost acceptance criteria).

Notes & references:
- Related playbook: CONFLUENCE-RET-142 (POS security patterns)
- Example infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/retail-adapters/pull/87 (adapter skeleton)

Notes-to-self: keep acceptance criteria strict but practical; encourage Summit to prioritize latency over richer context in first pilot to reduce risk.

Document history:
